solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shout when taking in boxer's last fight

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so one piece goes within the other
last points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: to bawl is to shout or cry loudly
the final letter of boxer

explanation.surface: A spectator yells as a boxer is drawn into a final bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough, noisy fight, usually a scuffle among several people.

clue.text: Nick another puzzle

blocks.note: first meaning: Old Nick, the Devil
second meaning: the pseudonym under which an Independent on Sunday advanced puzzle was published

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a verb meaning steal; it is Old Nick, the Devil. The other sense is a sister puzzle in the same newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Beelzebub is a name for the Devil, and it was also the title of the Independent on Sunday's harder barred-grid crossword.

clue.text: Skilful amateur supported by section of university in short

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for amateur
dept is the short form of department

explanation.surface: A talented amateur is backed by a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supported by' means the first piece sits above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly proficient or expert at something.

clue.text: Brief relay arranged to carry what's newsy essentially

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters are put into a fresh order
carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside
the essence of a word is its very centre, so take the middle letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the central letter of newsy

explanation.surface: A short relay set up to pass on the heart of the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective meaning short; it is the noun, a barrister's slang name.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a brief is a lawyer, especially a barrister handling a criminal case.

clue.text: Satirical work disowning society with conspicuous wealth? It's raising petty objections

indicators.note: disowning something means casting it off, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a squib is a short satirical piece of writing
S is the abbreviation for society
bling is showy jewellery or flashy wealth

explanation.surface: A satire stripped of high society and showy riches turns out to be mere nitpicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satirical work' tempts toward lampoon or skit; only the less common squib, which happens to begin with the society letter, fits the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Quibbling is the act of making trivial complaints or arguing over minor points.

clue.text: Clever comment from French team barring outsiders

indicators.note: barring the outsiders means excluding the outer letters at each end

blocks.note: équipe is French for team

explanation.surface: A witty remark from a French side that excludes foreign players.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a witty, clever remark or one-liner.

clue.text: Rising sun I represented with force? Not at first

indicators.note: represented is read as re-presented, put forward in a new form
not at first means the opening letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
urgency is pressing force or insistence

explanation.surface: Someone depicts a rising sun forcefully, though not initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising sun' reads as one phrase, but 'Rising' alone is the definition, the noun for a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a rebellion or revolt, the same as an insurgency against authority.

clue.text: Fuss university circle raised over expression of laughter

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
an orb is a sphere or circle
ha-ha is the written sound of laughing

explanation.surface: A university circle kicks up a fuss over someone's laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A brouhaha is a noisy commotion or excited uproar over something.

clue.text: Independent having a clue not cracked? That calls for graft

indicators.note: cracked suggests broken apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver who can't crack a clue faces some hard graft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graft' suggests hard work, but here it is the gardener's or surgeon's graft.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate originally meant to graft a bud into a plant, and later to introduce a vaccine into the body.

clue.text: Grand bird circling bay's entrance – and another

definitions.note: stands for another bird, after the bird in the wordplay

indicators.note: circling means going round, so one word surrounds the letter
the entrance to a word is its first letter

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a ree is a female ruff, a wading bird
the opening letter of bay

explanation.surface: A fine bird circles the mouth of a bay, followed by a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: The ree, a female ruff, is a crossword staple. 'Another' is the definition: a second bird besides the ree.
explanation.definitionFit: A grebe is a diving waterbird with lobed toes, so it is indeed a further bird.

clue.text: In borders of embassies, see wild variegated plant

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the frame made by the border letters
the borders of a word are its outermost letters, first and last
variegated means patchily mixed in colour, suggesting letters mixed up

blocks.note: the first and last letters of embassies
the words taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Diplomats notice a wild, many-coloured plant growing along the edges of embassy grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'variegated' does the mixing, leaving just 'plant' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Edelweiss is an alpine flowering herb with woolly white bracts, famous as a symbol of Switzerland and Austria.

clue.text: Place once for convicts with a certain bracing atmosphere

blocks.note: Oz is Australia, where Britain once transported convicts
one as in 'a certain person', 'one Mr Smith'

explanation.surface: A former penal colony is said to have a certain invigorating air.
explanation.walkthrough: Oz is informal for Australia, which served as a British penal colony in the 18th and 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popularly used for fresh, invigorating seaside air, though strictly it is a form of oxygen.

clue.text: Spot woman's stringed instrument

blocks.note: a zit is a pimple or spot
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone notices a woman's string instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a flat stringed instrument played horizontally by plucking, as in folk music of central Europe.

clue.text: Cinematic venue you once found in violent eras

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it
violent suggests turbulence that throws the letters into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
thou is the archaic word for you

explanation.surface: A picture house where you might once have watched films set in brutal ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An arthouse is a cinema that screens independent or foreign films rather than mainstream releases.

clue.text: Check Indian garment I rejected in general at a fixed price

indicators.note: rejected means thrown out, so the letter named is removed
in places the shortened garment inside the general's name

blocks.note: a tab is a bill or check in a restaurant
Robert E Lee was a Confederate general
a dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill, a discarded Indian garment, a general and a fixed charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The general is Robert E. Lee of the American Civil War, a crossword favourite; a dhoti is the wrapped cloth worn by many Indian men.
explanation.definitionFit: Table d'hôte describes a set menu served at a fixed price, as opposed to à la carte.

clue.text: Timeless bathroom feature to remain

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, and being without time means dropping that letter

blocks.note: a bidet is a low basin for washing found in some bathrooms

explanation.surface: A classic bathroom fitting is here to stay forever.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time, so BIDET loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: To bide is an old-fashioned verb for staying or waiting, as in 'bide your time'.

clue.text: Fellow, a Swiss hero, with love for sculptor

blocks.note: a don is a university fellow
taken as written
William Tell is the Swiss folk hero
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A fellow puts a Swiss legend together with love to make an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was an Italian Renaissance sculptor, famed for his bronze David.

clue.text: Footballer struck the bar in blustery conditions

indicators.note: struck suggests something knocked about and rearranged
in places one set of letters inside another word

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer hits the crossbar on a windy day.
explanation.walkthrough: Gareth Bale is a Welsh footballer who played for Tottenham and Real Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Gareth Bale is a famous professional player of association football, so he is an example of the category.

clue.text: Fat gained without exertion?

blocks.note: surface reading: putting on body fat without exercising
setter's reading: a fat sum, as in a fat cheque, earned with no effort

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like weight gain from idleness; fat here is a large sum of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is income gained without real effort or work.

clue.text: What's not seen by house viewers?

definitions.text: What's not seen by house viewers?

blocks.clueFragment: What's not seen by house viewers?
blocks.note: surface reading: rooms a prospective buyer does not see on a viewing
setter's reading: the audience in a theatre, who cannot see what happens behind the scenes

explanation.walkthrough: House viewers sound like property buyers; the house is a theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage describes what happens out of sight of the audience, in the wings or backstage.

clue.text: Recall knight and star defending inferior actor

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
defending something means surrounding and guarding it, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a celeb is a celebrity or star
naff is British slang for cheap, tacky or second-rate
K is the abbreviation for knight, as in KBE

explanation.surface: Someone remembers a knight and a star protecting a poor performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' reverses only the star, not the whole clue. Naff is British slang for tacky or lame, and K for knight comes from honours like KBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Affleck is an American film star and director, an example of a performer on screen.

clue.text: Aid for viewing French town

blocks.note: first meaning: a curved glass that focuses light
second meaning: a town in northern France, in the Pas-de-Calais

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a tourist aid for seeing a French town; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens is the optical piece in glasses or cameras, and Lens is also a mining town known for its football club.

clue.text: Identify guilt in fellow destabilising reign

indicators.note: destabilising means unsettling, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone blames a man for undermining a monarch's rule.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger someone is slang for accusing or informing on them as the culprit.

clue.text: Terrible disaster largely associated with European agricultural policy

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly disordered, so the letters are rearranged
largely means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: taken as written, to be trimmed
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A farming policy from Europe is branded a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: DISASTER loses its last letter and gains E before the shuffle. Set-aside was the EU scheme paying farmers to leave land uncultivated.
explanation.definitionFit: Set-aside was a European Union scheme that paid farmers to take land out of production to cut surpluses.

clue.text: Fashion feature associated with country walks, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a stile is a step for climbing over a fence on a footpath

explanation.surface: Fashion's place on rural rambles, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: Style and fashion both mean the current trend in dress or design.

clue.text: Bread, perhaps, model firm gets first to make

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: to sit is to pose as a model
CO is the abbreviation for company
the opening letter of make

explanation.surface: A baker's model firm gets around to making bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' looks like food, but it is the title of a British TV comedy from the 1980s about a Liverpool family.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread was a BBC situation comedy, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Educational setting devoid of pressure for French writer

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: a campus is the grounds of a university or college
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A stress-free college for a French author.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Camus was a French novelist and philosopher, author of The Outsider.

clue.text: Leave character on stage

blocks.note: first meaning: to depart or separate
second meaning: an actor's role

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a character making an exit; the two senses are a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to go away from someone, and a part is a role played by an actor.

clue.text: A lot of university volunteers noted conference site

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not the whole, so the word is cut short

blocks.note: Yale is an American Ivy League university
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Many volunteers at a university are noted as attending a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: YALE loses its last letter. The TA, or Territorial Army, is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta in Crimea hosted the 1945 meeting of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin to plan postwar Europe.

clue.text: Freedom of movement in ME country for one used to marching?

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

blocks.note: Oman is a country in the Middle East, abbreviated ME
range is the scope or freedom to move about

explanation.surface: Free movement in a Middle Eastern country for someone accustomed to parades.
explanation.walkthrough: An Orangeman is a member of the Orange Order, a Protestant fraternity in Northern Ireland known for its annual parades.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Orange Order are famous for their traditional summer marches, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Activity to form secret union?

blocks.note: surface reading: clandestine organising, as of an underground trade union
setter's reading: a marriage made in secret by running away together

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests covert labour organising; the union is a marriage, made by a couple running off together.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running away secretly to get married, usually without parental consent.

clue.text: Where litter can be seen after sport, showing sign of inactivity?

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
a litter of piglets is found in a pigsty

explanation.surface: Rubbish appears after a game, suggesting the ground has been neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' suggests rubbish, but it is a brood of piglets. 'After' places the pen after the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rusty means out of practice, skills dulled from lack of use, like corroded unused metal.
